title: runs/<run_id>/log.json — what an execution left behind (4.6, 4.6.9)
description: Not a card: the operator's record of one run. Derived from the artifact microscope_agent/src/operator.py already writes, not invented alongside it. Until this existed the file carried neither `card` nor `artifact`, so the collector skipped it and every check that names a run log -- 14, 15, 23, 37 -- had nothing to read and reported PENDING forever. The cost of that is specific: command provenance and the time base are the two things a run log exists to prove, and neither was being checked. The simulation side has no orchestrator and no device registry (4.6.8), so the fields that come from one are optional here; what is required is what both sides must answer for.

plan_id.description: the plan this run carried out. A run exists because a plan did (4.6) -- with one exception, settled 2026-09-24 (11-21): a PREPARATORY run carries null here, and then must carry `no_plan_because` and `approved_commands`, may dispatch nothing to the motion set, and produces no result card and no KB entry of its own. Its numbers reach the record only when a later plan cites its run_id as an input. Check 85 holds the parts a schema cannot: the motion set, and what cites the run. null is never a missing value: it is the statement that no plan governed this run, and the schema refuses it without the two fields that make that statement honest.

revision.description: the plan revision. An approval names (plan_id, revision), so a run that cannot say which revision it ran cannot be matched to one (6.1). null exactly when plan_id is null: a preparatory run has no plan and so no revision of one

approval.description: null id and kind is the honest state of a Tier 0-1 run: it needed no approval card, and saying so is different from failing to record one (6).

file.description: the approval file that authorised this run, by its path and the sha256 of its raw bytes, as the reader read it (plan.md 15.1 item 4). An approval binds from disk the moment it is there, before anyone commits it, so this is what leaves a trace of an approval that was never committed. Required when id is not null from card 087 on; run logs written before carry no file, and the schema cannot tell their dates, so it is optional here and the runtime's tests hold it

signed_through.description: copied from the approval when it was signed through the console

safety_policy_version.description: which envelope/safety.json was in force. Policy changes, and a run has to say which policy it ran under or the record cannot be read back later (2.1)

stop_criteria.description: ids of the monitors compiled from the plan. Stopping is a comparison against these, not a judgement (4.6.1)

t0_wall.description: wall-clock at t0, ISO 8601. Places the run in history; it does not order events

t0_mono.description: the monotonic origin every event offset is measured from (4.6.9)

backend.description: which backend ran it. mock is a first-class value: a plan runs unchanged on mock and on the engine, and that is the working definition of reproducibility (4.6.5)

registry_source.description: instrument side only: where the device registry was read from. Absent on the simulation side, which has no devices/ (4.6.8)

ended.description: how the run ended, the same word its events.jsonl's run_ended carries (card 057). Optional, because logs written before 2026-10-07 do not carry it. `refused` means the operator refused the run inside operator.run before any command went out: check 15 then asks for no approval, since refusing does nothing, and fails the log if any command was dispatched. Before this field, a run refused inside operator.run left events.jsonl and no log.json, which check 15 could only call pending for ever (card 065)

refusal.description: why the run was refused, as the operator said it. Required when `ended` is `refused`

plan_path.description:
The plan file this run actually opened, repo-relative. `plan_id` and `revision` are copied from inside the card and agree with themselves whichever file was opened, so until 3eda760 nothing in a run record could distinguish 'ran revision 1 deliberately' from 'ran revision 1 because operator.py built the filename without a revision and could not see revision 2'. That second case ran the discarded experiment and finished green (tasks/009).

Optional, because three runs predate the field and P1 does not rewrite them; absent means the record cannot make that distinction, which is a fact about the record and not a defect in it. The operator now refuses a mismatch between the filename and the card's own `revision` at the one point where both are in hand, so this field and that refusal are two halves: the refusal stops the pair from lying, this says which file the pair came from.

console_item.description: a run of another login's question only (plan.md 7.1.1 rule 9; microscope card 089, simulation card 028): the console inbox item the runner read to confirm the question was asked, as it read it -- its path, the sha256 of its raw bytes, its ids, and each attachment with the sha256 it checked. Check 91 requires it on a run whose plan carries a -c question id and refuses it on any other, and holds its sha256 to the item's bytes in the tree. Optional in the schema because a run log carries no question id of its own; the plan it names does.

no_plan_because.description: a preparatory run only: why no plan governed it, in words. Required with plan_id null and refused without it, so the field cannot be carried by a run that had a plan. The first one (2026-09-24) had none that fit: the only pre-measurement plan was 100x oil with software motion, and a 20x revision citing its axis ranges would have laundered them. A made-up plan_id to satisfy the old schema would have been a record claiming a plan that did not exist

approved_commands.description: a preparatory run only: the command list the person approved before any light, by path and sha256. It stands where a plan's scope approval would (11-21 condition 2). The path may lie outside the repository -- the first one sat beside its frames -- so check 85 verifies the hash when the file is readable from where the check runs and says so when it is not

approved_by.description: who approved, in words, as the approval was given

not_dispatched.description: a preparatory run only: that this run did not come through the plan dispatcher, and why, in words. Card 033 section 3b made this a condition of the first one, and that session wrote it here before this field existed; the field exists so the statement can stay where it was written rather than be moved to fit. Refused beside a plan_id, like the other two preparatory fields

event.description: One thing that happened, offset against the run's own t0.

t_mono.description: offset from t0_mono. Every event carries one, or the log cannot be put on a single timeline (check 37)

time_base.description: where this offset came from. software orders the log and nothing else: it carries OS scheduling jitter of milliseconds. A time a physical value depends on comes from a trigger counter or a device timestamp, and check 37 is what holds that line (4.6.9)

from.description: the plan.json field path this event was derived from. Commands are derived, never composed (4.6.1)

verification.description:
Whether the instrument was asked to confirm this command took effect. 4.6.6.1 rule 3 put its rule on this field and nothing carried it until 2026-09-20: the subsection says the run record carries `verification: none` for a channel that cannot be confirmed, and no such field existed. A rule written with nothing to hold it is the class counted most often that day.

`readback` means the channel's state was QUERIED AFTER the command and matched what was commanded. A return code is not a read-back: on the Tweez 300 a zero means the GUI accepted the text, and six distinct ways a command can be ignored all return zero (tweez300_reports_nothing_back, E3). An acknowledgement is `none`.

OPTIONAL ON PURPOSE, and check 66 rather than this schema is what requires it. Which actions need a read-back depends on reversibility, and reversibility lives on the plan's actions[] where a run log cannot see it -- an irreversible action requires one, a reversible one may legitimately go without. Leaving it out of `required` also keeps the two run logs written before the field existed valid, which is the honest reading: nothing asked them to record a read-back, so their silence is not a claim.

anyOf.description: parameters as sent. Each one names the field it came from, so a number in a command can be traced to the card that justified it (check 14).

from.description: field path in plan.json, e.g. numbers[exposure_time]. A parameter that cannot name its origin does not go out

anyOf.description: A TRAP STEP's params (2026-09-25, first planned trap run, run-20260925-004): the literal commands sent to the Tweez300, and the plan step they were derived from. Not the named-number form, because a tweezers command is text on a wire and not a set of graded numbers; recording exactly what went out is the record. Provenance is kept: `step.from` names the plan field, trap_steps.steps[<id>], as the named-number form's `from` does. Allowed only on an event whose channel is optical_tweezers.

params.description: parameters as sent. Each one names the field it came from, so a number in a command can be traced to the card that justified it (check 14). Or, on an optical_tweezers event, a trap step's literal commands and source step.

deletion.description:
A trajectory's positions were removed from this run directory (4.3.2, 2026-09-22). Deletion is the one operation that destroys the evidence for its own justification, so this records which DECLARED thing fired rather than why someone thought it should go.

It lives on a log event and not in trajectory_meta.json because that file has no schema: section 4 names it as an output and contracts/schemas/ does not hold it, so a deletion recorded there would be prose in an untyped file -- the defect this policy exists to avoid, inside the clause meant to preserve a record. The log is already an append-only record with a schema, and 13.1 put the watcher's output there for the same reason. trajectory_meta.json keeps saying what the trajectory WAS -- frames, steps, maximum displacement, stop reason -- which is what survives the data.

what.description: repo-relative paths removed, as they were named before removal

triggered_by.description: The declared thing that fired. There is deliberately NO free-text reason field: a sentence here would make the trigger a verdict the writer chooses, which is the shape check 6 and check 72 exist to stop, and deletion is its most expensive version because a wrong claim leaves something to read and a deleted trajectory leaves nothing. The reason is the criterion's own `statement` in the plan, by reference -- the same move as `estimation` naming the vocabulary instead of copying it.

kind.description: a stop/success criterion the plan declared before the run, or a named assumption falsifier that fired

declared_in.description: the plan card id and revision that declared it, e.g. plan-sim-20260917-001-r3. The revision is the load-bearing half: an opinion formed after a run has to become a declared criterion in a NEW revision before it can delete anything, and this field is where that shows.

observed_number.description: name of the number that failed it, when the criterion compares one

recorded_in.description:
Repo-relative path of the artifact that records this falsifier firing. Required when `kind` is `falsifier` and refused otherwise.

A falsifier's SENTENCE cannot be recomputed -- it says what would kill an assumption, and whether it happened is usually a fact outside the card, the way a_cost_reference was fired by a wall clock. But the fact is IN THE TREE, so the deletion names where and check 77 resolves the pointer. Without this the two paths to one irreversible act cost differently, and the uncheckable one is the one that gets used -- not from malice but from friction. Architecture ruled it on 2026-09-22, against this seat's own reading that a falsifier is simply not the recomputable kind.

watcher.description: The run-time watcher's payload (plan.md 13.4, shadow mode; added 2026-10-17 by manager-microscope-20261003-1). Carried only by the five watcher_* events, each with its own shape below. A WATCHER EVENT IS NEVER A COMMAND: none carries channel, action, params or verification, so nothing reads one as a command (check 14). Its probabilities are SIGNALS, ungraded, and never enter numbers[] (13.1 item 2: a model's number is E6). No threshold turns an answer into an action, and there is no would-have-done field, because no threshold is chosen (11-2).

judgement.description: the payload of judgement_asked (a request) and judgement_answered (a response), plan.md 13.5; never a command. Named judgement, not decision, because a `decision` event already records the person's own decisions in bench logs

buffer.description: what a stop saved from the rolling pre-stop buffer (plan.md 4.6.1). Written after the abort completed, never before it

recorded_rate_hz.description: the rate the run's own acquisition delivered, measured from the frames kept; null when fewer than two frames

path.description: the saved raw frames, kept whole in the run folder

judgements.description: the payload of judgements_started and judgements_off (plan.md 13.5), each with its own shape below: whether the run asks the plan's judgements at all, and by which backend. Never a command

derivation.description: the payload of a derivation event (plan.md 15.1 item 10): how every number in the plan was used before anything moved. Never a command

allOf.$comment: a watcher event is never a command (plan.md 13.4 item 6)
a watcher-labelled snapshot is read() on every channel this run opened, recorded for every reader; a channel not read at that tick says why inside states, never its last value
a judgement event is never a command (plan.md 13.5)
saving the buffer is a record, never a command (4.6.1)

why.description: length_zero: the plan wrote length_s 0, so nothing was kept, by the plan's own word. no_frames: the ring was empty when the stop came. no_run_folder: the run had no folder to save into. save_failed: the write raised; recorded once, never retried, because a retry could only come after the abort and must reach no light

frames.description: frames saved: always 0 here. Top level and not under `buffer`, because `buffer` is the saved event's alone

allOf.$comment: a stop that kept nothing says so and why (4.6.1: zero is allowed only if written, and an unsaved buffer must be told from a saved one). Added 2026-10-22 by manager-microscope-20261003-1 from the runtime seat's card 082 report, which needed the event and found none
added 2026-10-22 by manager-microscope-20261003-1 in the shape card 081 (99c02ddb) writes; a judgements record is never a command
added 2026-10-22 by manager-microscope-20261003-1 in the shape card 081 (99c02ddb) writes; a judgements record is never a command
added 2026-10-27 by manager-microscope-20261003-1 for card 095 (plan.md 15.1 item 10); a derivation record is never a command

backend.description: who answered. kind none asks nobody; test_double is a deterministic stand-in for mock runs, NOT A MODEL, and says so in every event it produces; model is a chosen model, which does not exist until the person chooses one (plan.md 11-27 (b))

options.description: the plan's option ids, in the plan's order

snapshot_t_mono.description: the t_mono of the watcher-labelled snapshot event this state rendered; null before the first one, and then the hardware side is rendered absent

image.description: each image-side value by name, with its unit, method and arguments and the frame it came from; a value with no input is null with absent_because, never zero

state_path.description: the rendered text, kept whole in the run folder, so the bytes replay from the records

asked.description: whether this state was put to the backend; false when one question was still in flight, or the backend is none

images.description: the reduced images given with this state, when the plan's frames.given is true (plan.md 13.4 item 6): each kept whole in the run folder beside the state text, so a decision replays with exactly what the model saw. Absent or empty when no image was given

stretch_limits.description: the stretch's limits for this frame, in ADU of the raw frame

images_not_given_because.description: when the plan gives images and none were made for this state, why: the conversion's refusal, verbatim. Absent when images were made or the plan gives none

options.description: the options as put to the backend, in that order

signals.description: what the backend returned, ungraded. Not numbers[]: a model's probability is E6 and may enter no card

backend.description: who answered. kind none asks nobody; test_double is a deterministic stand-in for mock runs, NOT A MODEL, and says so in every event it produces; model is a chosen model, which does not exist until the person chooses one (plan.md 11-27 (b))

prompt_version.description: versioned by judgement and plan (13.5), so the answer replays

why.description: image_conversion_refused: the plan gives images and this tick's conversion refused (a gap camera ceiling, for one), so the question is NOT asked text-only. A text-only answer under a plan that gives images would land in the wrong column of the text-only versus text-plus-images comparison that decides whether the picture adds anything (plan.md 13.4 item 9; architecture-office-20261017-1, 2026-10-19)

judgements_started.description: recorded right after run_started when the plan declares a judgements block that can be asked: who answers and at which points. A plan with no block records neither this nor judgements_off

questions_version.description: the version of the fixed question texts

judgements_off.description: the plan declared a judgements block and none of it is asked; the run goes on, because the judgements record only

detail.description: what refused the block, naming the field

derivation.description: One record per plan run, written at derivation and before the first command (plan.md 15.1 item 10, card 095). Every action parameter is sorted into exactly one class, every selector is a setting or a required state, and every number nothing uses is listed rather than dropped in silence. Added 2026-10-27 by manager-microscope-20261003-1 for card 095. The unused list is exactly what validate.unused_numbers gives for the plan, and check 97 holds it there; the console's sign dialog applies the same rule to the plan before any run exists, tested on the unused_numbers_case examples.

plan_hash.description: the plan_hash of the card the operator derived from, computed as an approval's is (status dropped). An id and revision name a card and not its contents, and a run that needed no approval carries no hash anywhere else, so this is what check 97 finds the card by; under a plan_approval it equals that approval's plan_hash

action.description: the plan action the parameter belongs to

from.description: the plan.json field path the number came from

binding.description: for a setting: the snapshot binding that names the label and property it is written to

verification.description: for a verb argument: what it is verified against, e.g. the frames the sequence returned

why.description: for a refused parameter: what it lacked, naming the binding or calibration

class.description: setting only on a device software may command; on any other device the selector is read and compared, never written

state.description: for a required state: the device's own state label the plan's value resolved to

unused_numbers.description: numbers the plan carries that no parameter, selector or limit uses. Listed, not refused
